findings.title: Full snapshot DeepEqual may be flaky with clock publication
findings.message: The new docs say clock publication can continue while analyses are read. If the snapshot includes clock or published state that changes on its own, deep-comparing the full snapshot taken earlier with `Wait` could make this test flaky. A failure would then not show that the queries mutated anything.
findings.suggestion: Compare only the fields that queries must not alter: revision, command_revision, document generation, history, selection, cursors and dirty flags. Alternatively, ensure the simulation clock is stopped before taking `before`.

findings.title: Tolerance with empty ID may appear in catalog
findings.message: `analysisCatalogLocked` adds a tolerance entry whenever `s.tolerance` is non-nil. If no tolerance run has been started, `view.ID` is likely empty. `analysisViewLocked` then matches `"" == ""` and succeeds, so the catalog lists a tolerance analysis with an empty ID. Clients cannot page that entry, because the page handler rejects empty IDs.
findings.suggestion: Only list the tolerance entry when it has a non-empty ID: `if s.tolerance != nil && s.tolerance.view.ID != ""`.

findings.title: Opaque reference in docs
findings.message: The phrase "The /279 package" is an unexplained internal reference. It is unclear what it means to readers of the public documentation.
findings.suggestion: Replace it with a clear version or release reference, or remove it.
findings.evidence: Service.Dispatch used by the UI and agents. The /279 package predates them.

findings.title: Ignored json.Marshal errors
findings.message: The errors from `json.Marshal` are discarded. If marshaling fails, the test sends an empty or invalid request, and the resulting failure points somewhere misleading.
findings.suggestion: Check the errors and call `t.Fatal` on failure.
findings.evidence:
params, _ := json.Marshal(q.params)
		request, _ := json.Marshal(workbench.Request{Version: 1, ID: q.command, Command: q.command, Params: params})

fix.before:
params, _ := json.Marshal(q.params)
		request, _ := json.Marshal(workbench.Request{Version: 1, ID: q.command, Command: q.command, Params: params})

findings.title: Inconsistent context usage
findings.message: The stdio path uses `context.Background()`, while the rest of the test uses `t.Context()`. That context is not cancelled when the test ends, and the two paths being compared get different contexts.
findings.suggestion: Use `t.Context()` for consistency. Then drop the `context` import, since it would no longer be used.

fix.before: if err = Stdio(context.Background(), s, bytes.NewReader(request), &a); err != nil {
fix.after: if err = Stdio(t.Context(), s, bytes.NewReader(request), &a); err != nil {

findings.title: Unhandled record type yields silently empty page
findings.message: The type switch over `record` has no default branch. If `analysisViewLocked` ever returns a new record type, the function returns a page with no rows. That page still carries a NextOffset and a Done flag computed from `summary.Rows`, so the data is silently dropped.
findings.suggestion: Add `default: return AnalysisPage{DocumentGeneration: s.documentGeneration}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported analysis record %T", record)` to fail loudly.

findings.title: Inconsistent nil/empty normalization in cloned slices
findings.message: The copies normalize nil and empty slices in opposite directions. `Values` always becomes a non-nil slice, even when the source is nil. `AC` always becomes nil, even when the source is a non-nil empty slice. Paged rows can therefore fail `reflect.DeepEqual` against the source, and JSON may encode `[]` where the source gives `null`, or the reverse. This depends on how producers fill these fields.
findings.suggestion: Preserve nil-ness, e.g. use `slices.Clone(point.Values)` and `slices.Clone(point.AC)`. The same applies to the RMS, Parameters and row Values copies.
findings.evidence:
v.Values = append([]float64{}, point.Values...)
			v.AC = append([]ACResponse(nil), point.AC...)
